sample_unit: oncology patients with ILD diagnosis codes

links.outcome: LLM PPV and yield versus 20 published claims-based algorithms on same cohort
links.effect: LLM PPV exceeded best algorithm without specialist-coding requirements (Algorithm 4) by 14.3 percentage points on average across 36 model–input evaluations; Qwen3-8B claims-only 89.8% PPV at 15.9% yield vs 86.7% at 4.9%.
links.quote: Across the 36 model–input evaluations, LLM PPV exceeded that of the best algorithm without specialist-coding requirements (Algorithm 4) by 14.3 percentage points on average.

links.outcome: Performance of LLMs on local historical data against pulmonologist-adjudicated reference standard
links.effect: In 309 patients adjudicated by two pulmonologists, zero-shot LLMs reached PPV up to 100.0% (Qwen3-14B, combined inputs, 24.3% yield) and extended the PPV–yield frontier of published algorithms.
links.quote: LLMs extended the PPV–yield frontier of the published algorithms with all three inputs.

unlisted_practices: Using zero-shot LLMs to replace rule-based claims phenotyping for drug-safety outcome identification
Quantifying downstream epidemiologic effect (odds ratio attenuation, sample size) of outcome misclassification

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs vs published rule-based algorithms for zero-shot clinical phenotyping/drug-safety surveillance on retrospective EHR notes and claims without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
